newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strong euro in France's interest - Delors.
newsitem.headline: Strong euro in France's interest - Delors.

text.p: Former European Commission president Jacques Delors said on Tuesday that a strong single European currency was in France's interest.
"France can only win with a strong currency, France can only win with a strong Europe because it will better be able to defend its interests," Delors told RTL radio in an interview.
Delors made the statement when asked if France and Germany could coexist happily within European economic union if they had different objectives for the union.

Delors said he was in favour of monetary stability but that he wanted a "stability council" or economic government to coordinate economic policy after the start of a single currency to exist with an independent European central bank.

"Why did I, first try to rid France of the the cancer of inflation, why, next, did I seek this economic and monetary union, it's because I, too, am in favour of stability and for the independence of the central bank," he said.

"But I often ask my German friends, in front of your independent Bundesbank would you like to have only a bureaucrat or bureaucrats? No, there is a government and that government counts and I am only asking for the extension of that mechanism to the European level," Delors said.
